card.name: Dose unit before a slash
card.fires_on: The unit (mg, mcg, units) right after a number when a slash follows to form a rate or concentration such as mg/kg, mg/mL or mcg/kg/min. It appears in dosing and dilution text.

modes.label: Weight-based dose
modes.description: The unit after a number is followed by /kg or /lb to give a dose per body weight.
modes.example: is 0.004<< mg>>/kg intravenously, not to exceed

modes.label: Concentration
modes.description: The unit after a number is followed by /mL to give the strength of a diluted solution.
modes.example: 40 mg/mL diluted to 0.6<< mg>>/mL with Dextrose Injection, US

modes.label: Infusion rate
modes.description: The unit is part of a per-kg, per-minute rate.

card.writes: It promotes time words such as minutes and seconds, which fits the per-minute part that can come after the slash.
card.plain: It marks the unit in a dose or concentration written with a slash, such as mg/kg or mg/mL, just before the per-weight, per-volume or per-time part.
